records.title: Baryon-Antibaryon Reconstruction at 50 MeV: Rest Masses and Cosmological Abundances
records.description: We reconstruct separate baryon and antibaryon equilibrium populations from fixed hadronic inventories, temperature, and a cosmological net-baryon-to-entropy constraint. An ideal hadron resonance gas is evaluated with PDG2014, PDG2020, and PDG2025 lists, retaining nominal masses and spin degeneracies. The baryon chemical potential is determined while mu_Q = mu_S = 0. At 50 MeV, PDG2025 yields 2.7261 × 10^30 baryons and 2.7172 × 10^30 antibaryons per cm³, with a net excess of 8.8765 × 10^27 cm⁻³. There are 306.1147 antibaryons per unit of net excess, and nucleons and antinucleons contribute 95.2176% of the total. The criterion n_antiB = n_B − n_antiB occurs at 38.203739 MeV, which rounds to the published reference of 38.2 MeV. Varying only the input eta = (6.12 ± 0.04) × 10^−10 gives 38.192814–38.214598 MeV. Comoving normalization relates these populations to an explicit present volume, while a rank test shows that the residual alone cannot identify a unique pair population or history. All 24 numerical checks and five archived CSV outputs were reproduced; a further momentum-integral calculation checks aggregate densities and entropy at two states. The baseline leaves nonzero net charge and strangeness. It provides a reproducible equilibrium reference; chemical-neutrality controls and kinetic evolution belong to the companion extension. Numerical agreement does not determine total physical uncertainty.

records.title: Symmetric Evaporation and Entropy Dilution of the Baryon Excess between 50 and 30 MeV
records.description: We quantify how thermal energy injection with no net baryon-number source changes a homogeneous expanding plasma between 50 and 30 MeV. A hypothetical population of nonrotating black holes is coupled to a thermal bath and an effective baryon-antibaryon production and annihilation equation. For an initial black-hole mass of 10^8 g and initial black-hole-to-plasma energy-density ratios f = 0, 0.01, 0.1, and 1, the reduced bath yields comoving plasma-entropy growth factors of 1.0000, 1.0109, 1.1093, and 2.0798. Net baryon number per entropy decreases inversely; the reduction is 51.92% for f = 1. With a common initial excess, the crossing n_antiB / (n_B − n_antiB) = 1 shifts from 38.205 to 37.974 MeV. With the initial excess adjusted to a common final yield, it instead shifts from 38.204 to 39.263 MeV. The complete PDG2025 hadron resonance gas gives 39.269 MeV for the latter f = 1 case. A local mass scan identifies a reheating trajectory with three crossings. Separate equilibrium calculations impose charge and strangeness neutrality with vanishing net lepton numbers; these constraints are not evolved in a coupled kinetic network. A repeated execution reproduced all 36 compared CSV files. The study quantifies the consequences of specified energy deposition and boundary conditions; the final baryon yield is an input constraint, and convergence tests do not determine total physical uncertainty.
